title: Go Modules & go.mod
intro: Go modules are how Go manages dependencies, and understanding go.mod is essential for working in any Go codebase. This module covers the module declaration in go.mod (module path convention — typically a GitHub URL like github.com/yourname/myapp), packages and imports (each directory is a package; the package name is declared at the top of every .go file; import paths are module-path + directory path), exported vs unexported identifiers (capitalised name = exported, accessible from other packages; lowercase = package-private), adding dependencies with go get (updates go.mod and go.sum), go mod tidy (removes unused dependencies, adds missing ones — the command you run before committing), the go.sum file (cryptographic hash of every dependency — always commit it), and the standard project layout conventions (cmd/ for entry points, internal/ for private code, pkg/ for reusable libraries). The interview question: 'what is the difference between go.mod and go.sum?'
